central_question: Can severing an attentive arc reduce experiential value when matched local feels and later reports show no distress or remembered loss?

terms.local_quality: Intrinsic phenomenal character attributed to an individual conscious phase.
terms.attentive_arc: A conscious orientation formed earlier is retained or taken up, shaped, and resolved in later awareness.
terms.experiential_achievement: A candidate positive good constituted by the organized conscious activity of carrying an attentive arc.
terms.mere_memory_like_state: A later representation or report-producing state that need not take up the actual earlier orientation.

argument.claim: An experiential episode can have temporal organization as well as local phenomenal qualities.
argument.support: The musical phrase case distinguishes hearing a developing phrase from a sequence of isolated tones; this is the phenomenon to analyze, not a verified theory.
argument.status: substantive premise requiring argument and closest-source check

argument.claim: Successfully carrying and fulfilling an attentive orientation may itself be a positive experiential achievement, without requiring a separate pleasant feeling.
argument.support: The value candidate is organized conscious uptake, rather than authorship, control, external success, or later knowledge.

argument.claim: A state that merely represents continuity or supports an accurate-sounding report does not necessarily carry forward the earlier orientation.
argument.support: The splice case stipulates a reset that ends the earlier orientation and a later memory-like state that does not reactivate or integrate it.
argument.status: case stipulation whose coherence and criteria require testing

argument.claim: If the arc is a positive experiential achievement, removing it can lower whole-episode value by omitting a good without adding a bad moment.
argument.support: Difference is between an achieved temporal good and its absence, not a hidden negative feeling.

argument.claim: A painless interruption that severs and fails to restore an attentive arc can reduce experiential episode value despite matched local qualities and later reports.
argument.qualification: No difference is claimed if the complete phenomenal organization, including all experienced temporal relations, is identical.

worked_case.name: The returned phrase
worked_case.continuous: Mira's opening expectation is carried, modified by intermediate notes, and resolved by the ending.
worked_case.spliced: A reset ends the earlier orientation; a memory-like state matches the apparent recollection and report, but does not take up the earlier orientation; the same ending follows.
held_fixed: matched local feelings at compared conscious moments
no knowledge of which history occurred
varied: whether the earlier orientation is actually taken up and structures the later experience
worked_case.scope_limit: If a memory trace or renewed attention genuinely restores the arc, the contrast is absent. Whether the causal uptake difference is experiential remains disputed.

objections.claim: A historical or causal difference without a phenomenal difference belongs to authenticity, agency, or external achievement, not experiential value.
objections.attribution: Concrete challenge separately attributed in the Astra assessment; the Sol assessment independently names agency/authenticity as the live rival.
objections.response: Matching local qualities and reports does not guarantee identical full temporal organization. The candidate good is conscious uptake itself, not external provenance. Concede that no difference is established if every phenomenal temporal relation is also identical.
objections.remaining_force: The response has not established that actual causal uptake is a constitutive experiential feature rather than a nonexperiential one.

objections.claim: The idea's stipulation may be incoherent: if apparent memory and later experience are fully matched, they may already realize the arc; if not, the case varies phenomenal structure.
objections.response: Specify that endpoint feelings and reports are matched, while actual uptake is varied. Treat the case as a test of whether this distinction is coherent, and reject the strong contrast if no defensible distinction remains.
objections.remaining_force: The exact boundary between representation, retention, reactivation, and integration remains unspecified.

objections.claim: The apparent value may depend on agency, authorship, or control rather than experience.
objections.response: Use passive listening as the core case and vary control/provenance independently in later tests.
objections.remaining_force: Attention may itself be a form of agency, and passive listening does not remove all agential value.

astra.content_summary: Asks whether missing continuity is an experiential good rather than a nonexperiential achievement when phenomenal difference is absent.
astra.response: Accepts this as decisive; narrows the claim to pointwise/local matching and reports, and concedes that full phenomenal-temporal identity removes the present argument.

sol.content_summary: Flags whether continuity is experiential or only agency/authenticity, and notes that originality and primary literature are unchecked.
sol.response: Agrees on the unresolved rival, proposes a passive case to reduce control/authorship confounds, and records source/originality checks as outstanding.

defeat_or_narrowing_conditions: Full phenomenal-temporal identity leaves only causal history, authenticity, or agency as grounds for preference.
A memory-like state is shown to restore the attentive arc, so interruption alone does not remove it.
Preference disappears when agency, provenance, knowledge, and external outcomes are controlled.
The value always reduces to pleasure, satisfaction, learning, or agency, leaving no distinct experiential achievement.
Ordinary lapses preserve or restore the arc, restricting the claim to genuine severance without re-integration.
